messages.content: Help me execute the test runner `runThis` with arguments to set the wait time to 2 minutes and output the logs to a specific print stream `testLogStream`, considering the debuggee name is 'TestDebuggee'?

function.name: runThis
function.description: Executes the test runner with provided arguments and a print stream for logging. It handles the debuggee binding, output redirection, and test execution flow. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

argv.description: An array of strings representing the command-line arguments, to include waittime and debuggeeName. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee This is Java Array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation.

out.description: The PrintStream to output the logs to. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning: We need to call the function runThis with argv array containing "-waitTime", "2", "-debuggeeName", "TestDebuggee". Wait time is 2 minutes? The argument expects string representation of integer? The description says waittime and debuggeeName. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -debuggeeName, TestDebuggee. So we pass waitTime as "2" (minutes). Also out param is a PrintStream object string representation. We have a specific print stream named testLogStream. So we need to pass out: "testLogStream". The function signature expects argv: string, out: string. But the description says argv is an array of strings. In the function type, argv: string. That seems wrong. But we should pass array representation. According to earlier instructions, we need to provide JSON with array elements as string representation. So we need to pass argv: ["-waitTime","2","-debuggeeName","TestDebuggee"] but each element is string representation. So we need to pass array of string representations. So we pass argv: ["-waitTime","2","-debuggeeName","TestDebuggee"]. And out: "testLogStream". Then we call the function.
